nodes.description: SigUtils internal pure helper that splits a 65-byte signature via assembly and recovers the signing address with ecrecover.
bytes32 message hash passed to SigUtils.ecrecover2.
Packed 65-byte signature (r,s,v) supplied by the caller of ecrecover2.
Raw ecrecover call: returns address(0) on malformed signatures and is invoked directly in the relay signature check.
Assembly-extracted signature parts r, s and v (v normalized to 27/28).
Constant burn address; if the stored signer equals it the wallet is permanently disabled (relay always throws).
Constant storage slot (keccak256 of 'marmo.wallet.signer') holding the wallet signer, read/written with assembly sload/sstore.
mapping(bytes32=>bytes32) packing canceled(1 bit) + block(95 bits) + relayer(160 bits) for each intent id; doubles as replay/cancellation guard.
Payable fallback that lets the wallet receive ETH.
Initializes the wallet signer; callable by anyone (msg.sender is not checked) as long as the signer slot is still empty.
Public view returning the stored signer read from SIGNER_SLOT via assembly.
View that decodes the intent receipt and returns the relayer address of an intent.
View that decodes the intent receipt and returns the block number at which the intent was relayed.
View that decodes the intent receipt and returns whether the intent was canceled.
Core entry point: recomputes the intent id, enforces replay/cancel checks, validates signer or signature, stores the receipt and delegatecalls _implementation with the id prepended to _data.
Marks an unrelayed intent as canceled; restricted to calls originating from the wallet itself (msg.sender == address(this)).
Internal pure assembly routine that packs canceled/block/relayer into one bytes32 receipt.
Internal pure assembly routine that unpacks a bytes32 receipt into canceled/block/relayer.
ERC721 receiver hook returning the magic selector 0x150b7a02.
msg.sender: used as the relay authorizer/signature fallback and stored as the intent relayer; also the only authority for cancel().
Block/time context: block.number is written into the intent receipt (timestamp/ordering dependency, 95-bit field).
delegatecall to the caller-supplied _implementation executed in the wallet's storage context; arbitrary external code runs before the result is checked.
Inline assembly sstore writing _signer into SIGNER_SLOT during an unauthenticated init().
Inline assembly bit packing/unpacking (shl/shr/or/and) of the receipt; the block field is truncated to 95 bits without validation.
Signer address supplied to init() and written into SIGNER_SLOT.
Intent id used as the intentReceipt lookup key in relayedBy().
Intent id used as the intentReceipt lookup key in relayedAt().
Intent id used as the intentReceipt lookup key in isCanceled().
Target contract address that relay() delegatecalls into.
Calldata forwarded to _implementation; its keccak256 hash is part of the intent id.
Signature over the intent id, verified through SigUtils.ecrecover2 when msg.sender is not the signer.
Intent id being canceled by the wallet itself.
Boolean cancel flag packed into bit 255 of the receipt.
Block number packed into bits 160-254 of the receipt (silently truncated if larger than 95 bits).
Relayer address packed into the low 160 bits of the receipt.
Raw bytes32 receipt to be unpacked.
Unnamed (operator, from, tokenId, data) arguments of the ERC721 receiver hook.
Local copy of SIGNER_SLOT used for the sload/sstore assembly operations in init().
Intent id computed as keccak256(abi.encodePacked(address(this), _implementation, keccak256(_data))).
Cached signer value read once from storage to avoid multiple sloads in relay().
Success flag returned by the delegatecall; on failure the return data is reverted verbatim.
Locals canceled and relayer produced by _decodeReceipt when a pre-existing receipt is found in relay().
Return locals _canceled, _block and _relayer produced by _decodeReceipt().

edges.reason: The message hash is passed into ecrecover as the signed digest.
Signature bytes are decoded and forwarded to ecrecover.
Assembly mload extracts r, s and v from the supplied signature bytes.
Locally decoded r, s, v are supplied to the ecrecover call.
The attacker-controlled _signer parameter flows straight into the sstore that defines the wallet signer.
Caller-supplied _implementation is the delegatecall target, giving arbitrary code execution in wallet storage context.
User-supplied _data is ABI-encoded with the intent id and forwarded to the delegatecall.
The relay signature parameter is recovered through ecrecover.
The locally computed intent id is passed as the hash to SigUtils.ecrecover2.
The relay signature parameter is passed to SigUtils.ecrecover2 for recovery.
msg.sender is the primary authorization input of relay(): signer equality check and receipt relayer value.
cancel() authorizes solely on msg.sender == address(this), a self-call based authority check.
msg.sender is packed into the intent receipt as the relayer field.
block.number (block/time context) is written into the receipt, making relayedAt time-dependent on miner-controllable ordering.
relay() writes the freshly encoded receipt for the intent id before the delegatecall (replay guard).
cancel() writes the canceled receipt into intentReceipt.
relayedBy() reads the stored receipt to return the relayer.
relayedAt() reads the stored receipt to return the block number.
isCanceled() reads the stored receipt to return the cancel bit.
The _id parameter is the mapping key used to look up the receipt in relayedBy().
The _id parameter is the mapping key used to look up the receipt in relayedAt().
The _id parameter is the mapping key used to look up the receipt in isCanceled().
The _id parameter keys both the receipt read and the canceled receipt write in cancel().
The raw receipt bytes are the assembly input of _decodeReceipt().
The canceled flag is shifted into bit 255 of the encoded receipt.
The block number is shifted into bits 160-254 of the encoded receipt without length validation.
The relayer address occupies the low 160 bits of the encoded receipt.
The encoded receipt produced by _encodeReceipt() is the value stored in intentReceipt.
The INVALID_ADDRESS constant gates relay(): a wallet whose signer equals it always reverts, disabling the wallet.
signer() sloads the signer value from SIGNER_SLOT.
init() writes the signer into SIGNER_SLOT.
init() copies the SIGNER_SLOT constant into a local for assembly use.
The local slot key drives the assembly sload/sstore in init().
The unauthenticated assembly sstore defines the value of the signer storage slot, i.e. wallet ownership.
ERC721 hook arguments are consumed (ignored) by onERC721Received.
init() unconditionally executes the assembly storage write; with no caller check anyone can seize an uninitialized wallet.
relay() reaches the delegatecall after signature checks, executing attacker-provided code with the wallet's storage.
relay() calls signer() to cache the stored signer.
relay() calls _decodeReceipt() when a non-zero receipt already exists.
relay() calls _encodeReceipt() to persist the new receipt.
relay() calls SigUtils.ecrecover2 when msg.sender is not the signer.
relayedBy() delegates decoding of the receipt to _decodeReceipt().
relayedAt() delegates decoding of the receipt to _decodeReceipt().
isCanceled() delegates decoding of the receipt to _decodeReceipt().
cancel() decodes the existing receipt before marking the intent canceled.
cancel() encodes the canceled receipt via _encodeReceipt().
_encodeReceipt() performs its packing through inline assembly bit operations.
_decodeReceipt() performs its unpacking through inline assembly bit operations.
SigUtils.ecrecover2 performs the raw ecrecover call.
The delegatecall transfers control to arbitrary external code inside the wallet's context after the receipt is written but before relay() returns, allowing reentrancy into relay()/cancel() flows.
